quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When braking and weight moves to the front of your bike, you should:

options.text: Slowly press harder on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry about weight transfer—it will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly press harder on the front brake.
questions.explanation: When braking, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake as weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the middle of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the middle of your lane. This discourages the other driver from coming back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Go faster.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane can be slippery when wet because of oil buildup. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. You should also slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: To react faster to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: Research shows that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
Brake the front tire too hard and do not brake the rear tire hard enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.

questions.question: You should not shift gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to shift gears.
The rough surface makes shifting harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles stop in about the same time as cars. However, wet pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Right away, release and then re-apply the front brake.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right away, release and then re-apply the front brake.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then smoothly apply it again.

questions.question: When loading items on your motorcycle:

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the back.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Put lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Store lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen better, avoid wind from other vehicles, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and avoid road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide you with an escape route in case of danger.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Meet U.S. DOT standards.
Fit snugly.
Have obvious defects.
Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious damage. Replace a helmet if it was worn during a crash.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.

options.text: Farther away, more slowly
Farther away, faster
Closer, more slowly
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, new riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Close to the back of the group.
At the end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: New riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to chase the group, and experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the animal.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Ride alongside the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: In traffic, motorcycles need:

options.text: Much less stopping distance than cars.
Less stopping distance than cars.
The same stopping distance as cars.
More stopping distance than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same stopping distance as cars.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the same distance to stop as a car does in traffic.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because it:

options.text: Discourages the passing driver from cutting back into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to cut back into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to finish passing as quickly as possible.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourages the passing driver to cut back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could make the passing driver return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake. Do not do both at the same time because braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to fall.

questions.question: A motorcycle windshield:

options.text: Can replace a face shield.
Can replace goggles.
Will not protect your eyes from wind.
Protects against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your shoulders.
Turn your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, no matter what speed you are traveling.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what following distance should you maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning
Lean in the direction you want to turn
Do not drag your feet on the road
Avoid looking at other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles
questions.explanation: Always watch for other traffic. Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of your turn. Never drag your feet on the road, as they could catch on something and cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane
In the center portion of your lane
In the right portion of your lane
On the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding too far to the right may encourage the passing vehicle to return to your lane too quickly.
